answer: A local-token reuse ledger makes duplication self-revealing: every action must spend a fresh token from the lagoon sensor, and reusing one token across agents creates a ledger collision. A cedar beacon adds an independent site class, so an identity cannot recycle tokens across sites without tripping the same collision rule. At the wharf gate, each extra identity must obtain a separately issued token, pay its fee, and wait for a fresh interval, raising duplicate cost.
